subject: Architecture
title: Vertical Farms: Skyscrapers That Feed Cities
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Vertical Farms: Skyscrapers That Feed Cities.

hook.text: What if skyscrapers grew food instead of housing offices? Vertical farms are making it real.

buildup.text: Indoor farms stack growing trays floor by floor, using LED lights and hydroponics instead of soil and sun.

discovery.text: A single vertical farm tower can grow the equivalent of 700 acres of traditional farmland.

twist.text: Energy costs are huge — LED lighting uses so much electricity that most vertical farms aren't profitable yet.

climax.text: Singapore, with almost no farmland, is investing heavily in vertical farms for food security.

punchline.text: Cities that can't spread out might grow up — literally.

quiz.question: What is the biggest challenge facing vertical farms today?
options: Plants cannot grow without natural sunlight
High energy costs for LED lighting make most unprofitable
Building codes prohibit farming inside skyscrapers
